## 2024-06-25 - std::vector initialization performance
**Learning:** Initializing a `std::vector<std::array<T, N>>` using a prototype array generated by `make_array<T, N>(0)` is significantly slower (~10-20% slower depending on size) than using value-initialization (e.g. `std::vector<std::array<T, N>>(size)`). Value initialization of vectors continuously zeroes out memory natively rather than explicitly constructing array elements and copying them into the allocated vector buffer one by one. Single `std::array` initializations are fast either way due to copy elision/optimization, but for vectors of arrays, native memory clearing is faster.
**Action:** Replace explicit prototype initialization `std::vector<std::array<T, N>> v(size, make_array<T, N>(0))` with native value-initialization `std::vector<std::array<T, N>> v(size)` when creating vectors of arrays that need to be zeroed. Similarly, for single `std::array` variables that just need zeroing, prefer the simpler `{}` initialization over custom template functions if it avoids unnecessary function template instantiations, although the performance difference is minimal after optimization.
